title: Find and Hand Back a Pointer
hints: `int** out` is a pointer to the caller's `int*`. `*out` *is* the caller's variable; `out` is just your local copy of its address. Writing `out = ...` changes nothing the caller can see.

`out = &arr[i];` will not compile (an `int*` is not an `int**`), and that error is the compiler pointing at the bug. You need `*out = &arr[i];` or `*out = arr + i;`. Two more things: `out` itself may be null, so guard every write with `if (out)`; and set `*out = nullptr` *before* searching so a miss never leaves a stale pointer behind.
